product_family: Playground - AI design studio (image/graphics generation, logos, merch, print-on-demand) and iOS app

certifications.name: SOC 2
certifications.proof_quote: No SOC 2 claim appears anywhere on the vendor's own domain (playground.com / playgroundai.com). The privacy policy only states a generic 'We implement physical, business and technical security measures to safeguard your personal information.' A third-party aggregator (Nudge Security) lists 'SOC 2 Compliant' but provides no clickable evidence and no link to a report.

certifications.name: ISO 27001
certifications.proof_quote: No ISO 27001 reference on any vendor-owned page. Third-party aggregator claims 'ISO 27001 Compliant' but offers no proof; not corroborated by the vendor.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No HIPAA reference on vendor pages; product is a consumer creative tool not positioned for PHI. Third-party aggregator lists 'HIPAA Compliant' without evidence; treated as unverified.

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: Vendor collects payment card data ('If you make a purchase, we collect credit card numbers, financial account information and other payment details') but makes no PCI statement; payments are likely handled by a processor. No PCI evidence on vendor domain.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No FedRAMP authorization exists on the FedRAMP Marketplace (the authoritative public registry of authorized cloud offerings) and none is claimed by the vendor. A third-party aggregator listing 'FedRamp Compliant' for a consumer AI design tool is implausible and is treated as a data-quality error, not evidence.

certifications.name: GDPR / CCPA (regulatory posture, not a certification)
certifications.proof_quote: "The following rights are granted under the European General Data Protection Regulation ('GDPR') and California Consumer Privacy Act ('CCPA'). Playground AI applies these rights to all users of our products, regardless of your location" and "we do not 'sell' personal information as defined by the CCPA and have not done so in the past 12 months."

privacy.ai_training_note: No explicit opt-out or 'we do not train on your data' statement. The Terms grant Playground a broad, perpetual license over user content for service improvement: "you grant to Playground AI ... a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, sublicensable, no-charge, royalty-free, irrevocable copyright license to use, copy, reproduce, process, adapt, modify ... text prompts and images you input into the Services, or Assets produced by the Service ... to use such Assets as needed to provide, maintain, promote and improve the Services." Separately, content is community-facing by default: "By default, your Assets may be publicly viewable and remixable by others." The privacy policy lists a purpose 'To improve and develop our Services.' Taken together this is consistent with using customer inputs/outputs to improve models. No business/enterprise carve-out (e.g. 'we do not train on paid/team content') was found.

security.name: Trust center / security page
security.value: None. playground.com/security and playground.com/trust both return HTTP 404. No dedicated security documentation published.

security.name: Encryption (at rest / in transit)
security.value: Not specified. Site is served over HTTPS, but no published statement on encryption at rest or in transit beyond a generic 'physical, business and technical security measures.'

security.name: Bug bounty / vulnerability disclosure
security.value: None found. No HackerOne/Bugcrowd program and no security.txt or VDP on the vendor domain. (A third-party aggregator shows empty 'Bug Bounty' / 'Vulnerability Disclosure' fields.)

security.name: Penetration testing
security.value: unknown - no public statement or report on the vendor domain.

security.name: Breach notification
security.value: Committed in policy: 'In the event of a security breach, we'll notify you so that you can take appropriate protective steps.'

security.name: Data retention
security.value: 'We only keep your personal information for as long as is needed ... After that, we destroy it unless required by law.' Retention periods are not quantified.

security.name: Children's data
security.value: Under-13 not permitted: 'We don't want your personal information if you're under 13.'

security.name: Cross-border transfer
security.value: 'your information may be stored in computers in other countries outside of your home country. By giving us information, you consent to this kind of information transfer.' No SCCs/specific region named.

products.name: Playground (web design studio)
products.category: AI image / graphics generation (logos, posters, stickers, social posts, mockups)
products.data_scope: Collects name, email, payment details, uploaded photos/files, content, IP/device, geolocation, usage. User Inputs and generated Outputs are covered by a broad perpetual license and are public+remixable by default.
products.notes: Free tier and paid subscription. Routes prompts to third-party image models (GPT Image 2, Nano Banana / Nano Banana Pro, Seedream) plus its own Playground v3 - those third parties are 'governed under their own privacy policies.'

products.name: Playground iOS app
products.data_scope: Same data practices as web per single privacy policy; may collect device geolocation depending on app settings.
products.notes: 4.9/5 across 5,400+ App Store ratings per marketing copy. Same Terms/Privacy apply.

products.name: Print-on-demand / merch store
products.category: E-commerce fulfillment (caps, hoodies, t-shirts, totes, socks)
products.data_scope: Adds payment and presumably shipping/fulfillment data for physical product orders.
products.notes: Physical goods imply a fulfillment processor in the data chain; not detailed in the policy.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium - free tier (no credit card to start) plus recurring paid subscription in USD; print-on-demand physical products sold separately.

flags: No trust center, no security page, no published encryption/pentest details (playground.com/security and /trust both 404).

No enterprise certification (SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / HIPAA) is claimed or evidenced on the vendor's own domain; a third-party aggregator (Nudge Security) asserts SOC 2/ISO/HIPAA/PCI/FedRAMP 'Compliant' with zero linked proof and an implausible FedRAMP claim - conflict between third-party claims and absence of vendor evidence.
Privacy-by-default is weak for business use: 'By default, your Assets may be publicly viewable and remixable by others' - inputs and outputs are public and community-remixable unless changed.

Broad, perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable license over user prompts and generated content, used to 'improve the Services' - effectively no opt-out from content reuse/model improvement; no paid/team data carve-out found.
No DPA, no SSO/enterprise controls documented, no named data region; consumer-grade processing posture only.
Liability capped at the greater of fees paid or USD 500; disputes via binding arbitration with class-action waiver (California law).
